additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent binge-eating episodes with a sense of loss of control, followed by recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors intended to prevent weight gain. It is typically accompanied by strong overvaluation of weight or shape, may fluctuate in severity over time, and is distinguished from binge-eating disorder by compensatory behaviors and from anorexia nervosa by the broader weight range in which it usually presents, though careful differential assessment is needed when weight is significantly low.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in the number of arguments with spouse (e.g., either a lot more or a lot less than usual regarding child rearing, personal habits)
patient.stressor: About one year and five months before evaluation, Linda and her husband began arguing much more often about household routines, her spontaneous projects, and the amount of food prepared for church, book club, and family gatherings. She initially responded by trying to impose strict control over eating and walking-club routines, but the tension at home increasingly gave way to private episodes of eating large amounts with a feeling that she could not stop, followed by purging and nonpurging efforts to prevent weight gain. Her concern about weight persisted even after others noticed she had become markedly thinner, making the problem feel shameful and out of step with the nurturing role she valued in her family and community. Linda eventually disclosed the pattern during a routine medical visit after her clinician asked directly about weight changes, and she accepted a referral for psychiatric treatment.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: What finally made me say something is that after I eat too much, I’ve been going upstairs and making myself throw up, then acting as if I’m just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: Even though my daughter and a woman from church have both told me I look too thin, I still panic if my skirt feels snug or the scale is up even a pound, as if I’ve somehow let myself become huge overnight.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: The next day I’ll skip breakfast and lunch or push myself to do extra laps with my walking group, not because I feel energetic, but because I’m trying to undo what I ate.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: When no one is in the kitchen, I can go through leftovers from a church supper, crackers, cheese, cookies, and whatever I baked for book club in one sitting, far more than I would ever serve myself at a meal.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like a switch flips and I’m watching myself keep eating while part of me is saying, ‘Linda, stop now,’ but my hands just keep reaching for more.

add_requirements.binge_eating_and_compensatory_behaviors_: Since last winter, there has hardly been a week when I haven’t had at least one of those private eating spells and then tried to make up for it by throwing up, skipping meals, or overdoing my walking.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I still get through my work at the optician’s, but I’m often preoccupied and worn down, and I’ve started avoiding some church and family meals because I’m afraid of how I’ll handle the food afterward.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about a year and five months, since the arguing at home over routines and gatherings really picked up.
